headline_marked: [[Two DGFI members dismissed, jailed]] for one year in Mohammadpur extortion case
headline: Two DGFI members dismissed, jailed for one year in Mohammadpur extortion case
summary: Two DGFI members have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each by a court martial for an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a businessman in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.
details: Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI), Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each.
This follows a court martial after their arrest over an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a businessman in Dhaka's Mohammadpur on October 25.
Intelligence sources confirmed that the allegations against the two were proven during the court martial proceedings. They were among six people arrested by police in connection with the incident.

The victim, motorcycle trader Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town, Mohammadpur, and asked to pay Tk 10 lakh. He had gone to the flat with an Ansar member who offered to help him buy a motorcycle.
Four people later entered the flat, confined him, and demanded money. Sharif also handed over Tk 70,000 he had brought to purchase the motorcycle before being assaulted and threatened again.

Around 3:00 am on October 25, Sharif was allegedly taken out of the flat and forced into a car. He managed to alert a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall near Shishu Hospital in Shyamoli, leading to the arrest of the six suspects and seizure of the car.

After being arrested in the case filed by the businessman with Mohammadpur Police Station, the two DGFI personnel were handed over to the army. They were subsequently tried under military law, resulting in their dismissal and imprisonment.

headline_marked: Students [[confine college principal for hours]] in Dhaka over fee dispute, demand resignation
headline: Students confine college principal for hours in Dhaka over fee dispute, demand resignation
summary: Students of Government College of Applied Human Science protested yesterday, confining their principal, Professor Dr Meherun Nessa, for hours, demanding her resignation over a dispute regarding a farewell program and alleged fees.
details: Students of Government College of Applied Human Science, formerly Home Economics College, staged a protest in Dhaka yesterday, confining Principal Professor Dr Meherun Nessa in her office for hours. They chanted slogans demanding her resignation.
The protest began around 10:30 AM, with students blocking the principal's office. Deputy Commissioner Moustak Sarker of DMP's Lalbagh division confirmed that she was rescued safely around midnight.

The dispute originated before the Durga Puja holidays over a farewell program for final-year postgraduate students. The program, initially scheduled to end at 10:00 PM, was extended until midnight at students' request but ultimately continued until 5:00 AM.

Following this, the principal cancelled the residential hall seats of two students who coordinated the event, citing the extended use of the auditorium. Students alleged she demanded Tk 12,600 for air-conditioning and electricity costs to reinstate their seats.

A postgraduate student, Tabassum, stated that the movement began due to the seat cancellations and the high fee demand. She emphasized that students cannot afford such an amount even after apologizing.
Principal Meherun Nessa disputed the students' account, stating she permitted the program only until midnight, not 5:00 AM. She admitted to cancelling the seats of two students out of anger.

The principal said she later showed leniency after apologies but insisted on disciplinary action to prevent future violations. She justified the fine, stating, "They wasted electricity for a long time, and I will collect the bill from them."
She also alleged that the protesting students had asked her to sign a resignation letter on a blank sheet of paper during the confinement.
